Retrieval Index
The complete retrieval index consisting of the unified knowledge graph and the embedding table, providing structural knowledge representation and dense vector space for cross-modal similarity search.<SEP>The Retrieval Index, denoted as T = (G, T), combines the unified knowledge graph and embedding table to provide both structural knowledge representation and dense vector space for cross-modal similarity search.

Unified Knowledge Graph
A comprehensive knowledge graph denoted as G = (ν, E) that captures both multimodal contextual relationships and text-based semantic connections after graph fusion.<SEP>The Unified Knowledge Graph, denoted as G, is a structural knowledge representation that encodes explicit relationships and multi-hop reasoning patterns across heterogeneous modalities.

Embedding Table
A comprehensive table that encompasses all components generated during the indexing process, mapping entities, relations, and chunks to dense representations.<SEP>The Embedding Table, denoted as τ, stores dense vector representations of knowledge components and enables semantic similarity search.

Cross-Modal Hybrid Retrieval
Cross-Modal Hybrid Retrieval is a mechanism that combines structural knowledge navigation with semantic similarity matching to enable effective retrieval across heterogeneous modalities. It leverages both a unified knowledge graph and an embedding table to perform efficient cross-modal similarity search, allowing textual queries to access non-textual content through shared embeddings. By integrating graph-based retrieval with cross-modal integration, the approach identifies relevant knowledge components for a given user query and supports reasoning over heterogeneous content.

This mechanism is employed by RAG-Anything, where it contributes to the system's effectiveness in long-document reasoning tasks. Within the RAG-Anything pipeline, cross-modal hybrid retrieval operates as a retrieval stage that follows the graph fusion step. Its contribution has been validated by ablation study results.

Modality-Aware Query Encoding
Modality-Aware Query Encoding performs query analysis to extract lexical cues and potential modality preferences, then computes a unified text embedding using the same encoder employed during indexing.

Structural Knowledge Navigation
Structural knowledge navigation is a component of the cross-modal hybrid retrieval mechanism that leverages explicit graph relationships to capture multi-hop reasoning patterns.<SEP>Structural Knowledge Navigation exploits structural properties encoded within the unified knowledge graph, employing keyword matching and entity recognition followed by strategic neighborhood expansion to capture explicit relationships and multi-hop reasoning patterns.<SEP>Structural Knowledge Navigation is a retrieval mechanism that interacts with the Knowledge Graph.<SEP>A retrieval capability supported by the union over V, E, and c_j, allowing navigation of structural knowledge elements.<SEP>Structural knowledge navigation is a component of the cross-modal hybrid retrieval architecture that enables leveraging explicit relationships across modalities.

Semantic Similarity Matching
Semantic similarity matching is a component of the cross-modal hybrid retrieval mechanism that employs dense vector representations to identify semantically relevant content.<SEP>Semantic Similarity Matching conducts dense vector similarity search between the query embedding and all components stored in the embedding table, enabling fine-grained semantic matching across all modalities.<SEP>Semantic Similarity Matching is a retrieval mechanism that interacts with the Vector Database.<SEP>A retrieval capability supported by the union over V, E, and c_j, allowing matching of knowledge components by semantic similarity.<SEP>Semantic similarity matching is a component of the cross-modal hybrid retrieval architecture that enables leveraging implicit semantic connections across modalities.

Candidate Pool Unification
Candidate Pool Unification combines retrieval candidates from both structural and semantic pathways into a comprehensive candidate pool for principled ranking.<SEP>Candidate pool unification is the process of merging retrieval results into a single pool for subsequent fusion and ranking.

Multi-Signal Fusion Scoring
Multi-Signal Fusion Scoring integrates structural importance from graph topology, semantic similarity scores from embedding space, and query-inferred modality preferences to produce final ranked candidates.<SEP>Multi-signal fusion scoring is the technique used to fuse and rank the unified candidate pool to produce the top-ranked retrieval candidates C*(q).

Hybrid Retrieval Integration
Hybrid Retrieval Integration leverages the complementary strengths of both knowledge graphs and dense representations to provide comprehensive coverage of relevant multimodal knowledge.

Synthesis Stage
The Synthesis Stage systematically combines retrieved multimodal knowledge into comprehensive, evidence-grounded responses by building structured textual context from top-ranked retrieval candidates.

Building Textual Context
Building Textual Context concatenates textual representations of all retrieved components, including entity summaries, relationship descriptions, and chunk contents, with appropriate delimiters to indicate modality types and hierarchical origins.

Multimodal Question Answering
Multimodal Question Answering requires preserving rich visual semantics while maintaining coherent grounding across heterogeneous knowledge sources.<SEP>Multimodal question answering is the core idea embodied by the equation, preserving rich visual semantics while maintaining coherent grounding across heterogeneous knowledge sources.

RAG
Traditional RAG methods rely on semantic similarity within single modalities and face significant limitations when dealing with multimodal documents.

User Query
A user query, denoted as q, is the input for which relevant knowledge components are identified during the retrieval stage.

Query Embedding
The Query Embedding, denoted as e_q, is a unified text embedding computed from the user query using the same encoder employed during indexing.

Structural Candidate Set
The Structural Candidate Set, denoted as C_str(q), contains relevant entities, relationships, and associated content chunks obtained through structural knowledge navigation.

Semantic Candidate Set
The Semantic Candidate Set, denoted as C_seman(q), contains the top-k most semantically similar chunks ranked by cosine similarity scores from semantic similarity matching.

Unified Candidate Pool
The Unified Candidate Pool, denoted as C(q), is the union of structural and semantic candidate sets, providing comprehensive coverage of both structurally and semantically relevant knowledge.

Final Ranked Candidates
The Final Ranked Candidates, denoted as C*(q), are the output of multi-signal fusion scoring that balance structural knowledge relationships with semantic relevance.

Embedding Function
The Embedding Function, denoted as (·), is tailored for each component type to generate embeddings for knowledge components.

Multimodal Documents
Multimodal Documents contain visual, mathematical, tabular, and textual elements with rich interconnections that traditional RAG methods fail to capture.<SEP>Documents containing text, figures, tables, and equations, from which atomic content chunks c_j are extracted.

Modality Preferences
Modality Preferences are potential preferences for specific modalities embedded within a user query, inferred through lexical cues such as terms like "figure," "chart," "table," or "equation."

Encoder
The Encoder is employed during indexing and reused for computing the query embedding to ensure consistency between query and knowledge representations.

Cosine Similarity
Cosine Similarity is used to rank the top-k most semantically similar chunks in the semantic similarity matching pathway.<SEP>A similarity measure used to compare queries and knowledge components within the unified vector space provided by the embedding table.

Language Model
The Language Model parses and reasons over heterogeneous knowledge from the structured textual context constructed during the synthesis stage.

Structural Importance is a relevance signal derived from graph topology used in multi-signal fusion scoring.

Semantic Similarity Scores

RAG-Anything
RAG-Anything is a unified, all-in-one retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework designed to reimagine multimodal knowledge representation and retrieval. It treats text, images, tables, and equations as first-class entities, reconceptualizing multimodal content as interconnected knowledge entities. The framework extends GraphRAG to all modalities and unifies heterogeneous multimodal knowledge by decomposing content into atomic content units.

At its core, RAG-Anything employs a dual-graph construction strategy, building both cross-modal and text-based knowledge graphs that are merged via entity alignment. This produces modality-aware graphs that preserve essential relationships within multimodal documents, enabling precise reasoning over complex layouts. Complementing this is a cross-modal hybrid retrieval mechanism, which together with the dual-graph approach forms the framework's central architecture for cross-modal retrieval and reasoning. The framework also includes a dense representation generation step in its indexing pipeline and constructs a cross-modal knowledge graph (as described by Equation 4). Additional features include context-aware multimodal prompting.

RAG-Anything demonstrates superior performance on long documents and complex multimodal layouts, particularly where relevant evidence is dispersed across multiple modalities and sections. It has been evaluated using the DocBench and MMLongBench benchmarks, including an ablation study on DocBench. On MMLongBench, it achieves the best results in information-dense domains such as Research Reports and Financial Reports, with consistent improvements across all document length categories: accuracy gains of 3.4 points for 11–50 pages, 9.3 points for 51–100 pages, and 7.9 points for 101–200 pages. It outperforms MM-GraphRAG on long-document reasoning tasks.

The framework excels at complex visual reasoning and tabular navigation by constructing structured graph representations of visual elements (such as bar plots) and tabular data, enabling precise alignment between visual and textual information. However, in documented failure cases, RAG-Anything produced an incorrect answer regarding the NER label generation sequence and failed to correctly interpret an irregular table in a cross-modal noise scenario. The framework's documentation also addresses challenges and future directions for multimodal RAG.

MM-GraphRAG
MM-GraphRAG is a baseline method that exhibits comparable performance to RAG-Anything on shorter documents but falls behind as document length grows, and only considers image modality entities.<SEP>MM-GraphRAG is a baseline framework that exhibits comparable performance to RAG-Anything on shorter documents but falls behind as document length grows.<SEP>MM-GraphRAG is a RAG method that exhibits comparable performance to RAG-Anything on shorter documents but falls behind as document length increases.<SEP>MM-GraphRAG is a RAG method that shows comparable performance to RAG-Anything on shorter documents but falls behind as document length increases.

DocBench
DocBench is a challenging multimodal Document Question Answering benchmark designed to evaluate model performance across varying document lengths and to validate the effectiveness of the RAG-Anything approach. It comprises 229 documents spanning five domains and document types, with an average length of 66 pages and approximately 46,377 tokens per document. The benchmark includes 1,102 expert-crafted question-answer pairs. Its documents encompass medium- to long-length materials across various domains, including legal, governmental, and financial files, with financial reports averaging 192 pages and news consisting of concise single-page newspapers; detailed statistics are provided in Table 5.

DocBench serves as an evaluation dataset for the RAG-Anything framework and its variants, enabling sophisticated visual interpretation and evidence-grounded response generation. On this benchmark, RAG-Anything outperforms MM-GraphRAG by over 13 points on documents exceeding 100 pages, a performance gap that expands dramatically at that document length. Representative cases from DocBench have been analyzed to demonstrate how RAG-Anything leverages structural information and intra-modal structures.

MMLongBench
MMLongBench is a challenging long-context multimodal document comprehension benchmark designed to evaluate document question answering and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frameworks. It comprises 135 documents spanning 7 document types, with an average length of 47.5 pages and 21,214 tokens per document, accompanied by 1,082 expert-annotated questions. The benchmark's document composition covers a broad spectrum of types and lengths, including research reports, tutorials, academic papers, guidebooks, brochures, and administrative files, with detailed dataset statistics summarized in Table 6, where it is referenced alongside DocBench.

MMLongBench serves as an evaluation platform for assessing method performance across seven document domains and across documents of varying lengths, measuring overall accuracy and enabling sophisticated visual interpretation and evidence-grounded response generation. It is notably used to validate the effectiveness of the RAG-Anything approach, which demonstrates consistent accuracy improvements across all document length categories and achieves the best results in information-dense domains such as Research Reports and Financial Reports, outperforming baselines like MM-GraphRAG.

Dual-Graph Construction
Dual-Graph Construction is a core architectural strategy and mechanism employed by RAG-Anything, designed to bridge cross-modal understanding with fine-grained textual semantics by building complementary knowledge graphs. It operates by constructing a cross-modal knowledge graph and a text-based knowledge graph, which are then merged through entity alignment to achieve a richer, unified knowledge representation. This approach captures both structural and cross-modal relationships within multimodal documents while preserving semantic alignment and structural context.

The technique is integrated within RAG-Anything's structured context injection mechanism, where it supports cross-page entity alignment. It is enabled as a subsequent process following the atomic units provided by document decomposition. Dual-Graph Construction contributes significantly to RAG-Anything's effectiveness in long-document reasoning tasks, and it is a component that is bypassed in the Chunk-Only variant of the system.

Chunk-Only

Reranker

GPT-4o-mini
GPT-4o-mini is a powerful multimodal language model with native text and image understanding capabilities and a 128K token context window. It serves as a backbone LLM and baseline in experimental frameworks, and is used to conduct all accuracy evaluations throughout these frameworks, ensuring consistent, reliable, and consistent assessment standards.

As a method, GPT-4o-mini was evaluated on the DocBench dataset, achieving an overall accuracy of 51.2%, and on MMLongBench, achieving an overall accuracy of 33.5%. As a baseline model, it demonstrated several incorrect responses across various tasks: it incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation in a multi-panel figure interpretation case; it incorrectly answered DKK 32,928 million for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020; it provided an incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15; and it incorrectly identified the BERT-to-BERT model with an AUPRC of 0.455 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. Additionally, GPT-4o-mini was evaluated in a multimodal RAG failure case, producing an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence, and in a cross-modal noise case, providing an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

LightRAG
LightRAG is a graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that integrates structured knowledge representation with dual-level retrieval mechanisms. It is an established text-centric extraction pipeline methodology referenced as a basis for constructing text-based knowledge graphs, and it employs a graph construction approach that uses sparsified indices to optimize structures for retrieval efficiency. As a baseline RAG framework, LightRAG is restricted to text-only content processing.

LightRAG has been evaluated on several benchmarks. On the DocBench dataset, it achieved an overall accuracy of 58.4% and led in the Law domain. On MMLongBench, it achieved an overall accuracy of 38.9%.

As a baseline model, LightRAG has also been assessed in various failure cases. It incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation in a multi-panel figure interpretation case, and it incorrectly answered DKK 11,503 million for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020. It provided a partially incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15, and it incorrectly identified the BERT + LSTM - Attention model with an AUPRC of 0.429 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. In a multimodal RAG failure case, it produced an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence, and in a cross-modal noise case, it provided an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

MMGraphRAG
MMGraphRAG is a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that constructs unified knowledge graphs spanning both textual and visual content, employing spectral clustering for multimodal entity analysis. It links scene graphs with textual representations, though this approach has been noted to suffer from structural blindness. As a baseline RAG framework, MMGraphRAG only adds basic image processing while treating tables and equations as plain text, thereby missing crucial structural information.

MMGraphRAG has been evaluated on several benchmarks. On the DocBench dataset, it achieved an overall accuracy of 61.0%, leading in the Academia, Government, and Unanswerable categories. On MMLongBench, it achieved an overall accuracy of 37.7%.

Beyond benchmark performance, MMGraphRAG has been examined in various failure and error cases. In a multi-panel figure interpretation case, it incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation. It incorrectly answered 11,503 million DKK for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020. It provided a partially incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15. It incorrectly identified the Bert-To-Bert model with an AUPRC of 0.708 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. In a multimodal RAG failure case, it produced an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence. In a cross-modal noise case, it provided an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

Equation (1)
Equation (1) is a LaTeX-formatted mathematical equation that formalizes the Multimodal Knowledge Unification process, stating that each knowledge source k_i from corpus K is decomposed into a set of n_i atomic content units {c_j}, where each unit c_j is a pair (t_j, x_j).

RAG-Anything Framework
The RAG-Anything framework is a system in which Equation (1) formalizes the Multimodal Knowledge Unification process.<SEP>The RAG-Anything framework is a system for cross-modal knowledge graph construction that transforms heterogeneous multimodal content into structured, retrievable knowledge.<SEP>The RAG-Anything framework is a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation system that defines the final response generation step through a mathematical equation.

Knowledge Source
A knowledge source k_i is an element of the corpus K that is decomposed into a set of n_i atomic content units.

Atomic Content Unit
An atomic content unit c_j is a pair (t_j, x_j) produced by decomposing a knowledge source, where t_j denotes the modality type and x_j represents the corresponding raw content.

Raw Content
Raw content x_j represents the content extracted in a modality-aware manner corresponding to a modality type.

Decompose
Decompose is the operation denoted by the arrow in Equation (1) that breaks each knowledge source into atomic content units.

Cross-Modal Retrieval
Cross-modal retrieval is a capability supported by the canonical decomposition defined in Equation (1), enabling retrieval and reasoning across different modalities.

Corpus
The corpus K is the collection of knowledge sources from which atomic content units are derived.

LaTeX
LaTeX is the format used for Equation (1), a typesetting system for mathematical notation.

Modality-Aware Extraction
Modality-aware extraction is the manner in which raw content x_j is extracted, respecting the specific characteristics of each modality.

Unified Multimodal Representation
Unified multimodal representation is the challenge directly addressed by Equation (1), which defines a canonical decomposition supporting cross-modal retrieval and reasoning.

Uniform Indexing And Retrieval
Uniform indexing and retrieval is the process to which atomic content units are amenable, ensuring each unit retains its modality-specific characteristics.

Query Q
The query q is the original input question that the Vision-Language Model conditions on when generating a response.

Textual Context P(q)
The textual context P(q) is constructed by concatenating textual representations of top-ranked retrieval candidates, including entity summaries, relationship descriptions, and chunk contents, with delimiters indicating modality and hierarchy.

Visual Artifacts V*(q)
The visual artifacts V*(q) are a set of dereferenced visual content recovered from multimodal chunks, ensuring authentic visual semantics are available for reasoning.

Retrieval-to-Synthesis Pipeline
The retrieval-to-synthesis pipeline is the overall process where hybrid retrieval yields a candidate pool that is fused and ranked, culminating in the synthesis stage that generates responses.

Dense Representations
Dense representations are one of the complementary knowledge sources whose strengths are leveraged in the synthesis stage of the framework.

C*(q)
C*(q) is the set of top-ranked retrieval candidates produced by fusing and ranking the unified candidate pool, whose textual representations are concatenated to form the textual context P(q).

Multimodal Chunks
Multimodal chunks are retrieval units corresponding to visual artifacts that are dereferenced to recover the visual content V*(q).

Equation (3)
Equation (3) is a LaTeX-formatted mathematical equation that defines the vertex set of the cross-modal knowledge graph as the union of multimodal entity nodes and intra-chunk entity sets.

Vertex Set
The vertex set, denoted by \tilde{V}, is the complete set of vertices in the cross-modal knowledge graph, formed as the union of multimodal entity nodes and intra-chunk entity sets.

Multimodal Entity Nodes
Multimodal entity nodes, denoted as {v_j^{mm}}_j, are anchor nodes each associated with a non-text atomic unit c_j such as an image, table, or equation.

Anchor Nodes
Anchor nodes v_j^{mm} are explicit multimodal entities that ground non-text content and serve as anchors in the cross-modal knowledge graph.

Intra-Chunk Entity Sets
Intra-chunk entity sets, denoted as \mathcal{V}_j, are fine-grained entities extracted from the textual description d_j^{chunk} of each non-text unit via the graph extraction routine R(·).

Non-Text Atomic Unit
A non-text atomic unit c_j is a content element such as an image, table, or equation, each associated with an anchor node and a textual description.

Textual Description
The textual description d_j^{chunk} is the generated text describing each non-text unit, from which intra-chunk entities are extracted.

Set-Theoretic Union Operation
The set-theoretic union operation combines the anchor nodes with all fine-grained entities identified within each non-text chunk to form the complete vertex set.

Belongs_to Edges
Belongs_to edges connect each anchor node to its associated intra-chunk entities, preserving modality-specific grounding.

Indexing
Indexing is a subsequent stage following graph fusion in the framework's pipeline.

Hybrid Retrieval
Hybrid retrieval is a subsequent stage that leverages the unified graph structure for cross-modal retrieval and reasoning.

Document Collection
The document collection is the set of documents over which the index j ranges, containing all non-text atomic units.

Modality-Specific Grounding
Modality-specific grounding is preserved by the belongs_to edges connecting each anchor node to its associated intra-chunk entities.

Cross-Modal Retrieval And Reasoning
Cross-modal retrieval and reasoning is enabled by the construction that contextualizes non-textual content by its textual neighborhood.

Cross-Modal Hybrid Retrieval Mechanism
Cross-modal hybrid retrieval is a mechanism used by RAG-Anything that is particularly effective for long-document reasoning tasks.

QA Pair Count

Long-Document Reasoning Tasks

Graph Extraction Operation
The graph extraction operation is defined by the equation (𝒱_j, ℰ_j) = R(d_j^{chunk}) and produces sets of intra-chunk entities and relations from non-text content units.

Equation (𝒱_j, ℰ_j) = R(d_j^{chunk})
The equation defines the core graph extraction operation, specifying that a routine R(·) processes a unit's description d_j^{chunk} to produce entity set 𝒱_j and relation set ℰ_j.

Non-Text Atomic Content Unit
A non-text atomic content unit c_j is an individual piece of content such as an image, table, or equation that is processed for graph extraction.

Description d_j^{chunk}
The description d_j^{chunk} is a textual representation generated by a multimodal large language model, optimized for cross-modal retrieval and computed using the unit's local neighborhood.

Relations ℰ_j
Relations ℰ_j are the set of relations among entities extracted from a non-text content unit's description.

Extraction Routine R(·)
The extraction routine R(·) performs entity and relation extraction on the derived description of a non-text unit, analogous to named entity recognition and relation extraction in text-based pipelines.

Multimodal Large Language Model
The multimodal large language model generates the textual description d_j^{chunk} for non-text content units.

Local Neighborhood C_j
The local neighborhood C_j = {c_k : |k - j| ≤ δ} is the context used to compute the description, where δ controls the contextual window size.

Multimodal Entity Node v_j^{mm}
The multimodal entity node v_j^{mm} anchors the extracted entities and relations via belongs_to edges, grounding non-textual content within its textual context.

Unified Knowledge Representation 𝒢 = (𝒱, ℰ)
The unified knowledge representation 𝒢 = (𝒱, ℰ) is formed by fusing the cross-modal and text-based knowledge graphs through entity alignment.

Dense Vector Space
The dense vector space is where extracted entities, relations, and atomic content chunks are embedded to enable efficient similarity-based retrieval.

Text-Only RAG Systems
Text-only RAG systems are limited by their inability to handle heterogeneous multimodal content, a limitation addressed by the RAG-Anything framework.

Similarity-Based Retrieval
Similarity-based retrieval is the efficient retrieval enabled by embedding extracted entities, relations, and atomic content chunks into a dense vector space.

Atomic Content Chunks
Atomic content chunks are the individual content units that, along with extracted entities and relations, are embedded into a dense vector space.
